The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Inside the FBI’s little-known annual crypto crime gathering. The Virtual Asset Technical Exchange brings together investigators, law enforcement officials, and crypto-security specialists to exchange intelligence on a wide range of crimes involving digital assets. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Crypto Long & Short: Inside the chain settling $150 billion of stablecoins a week. Tron launched as a content-distribution project and has become the settlement layer for a large share of the world's USDT, processing roughly $150 billion to $190 billion of stablecoin transfers a week. Josh Olszewicz of Canary Capital breaks down how the network's economics work and what stablecoin regulation could do to the thesis. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Bitcoin's $16 billion quarterly options settlement arrives with a 'call-heavy' book. Nearly $18 billion in bitcoin and ether options will expire on Friday, potentially reshaping dealer hedging flows and short-term volatility. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

MoonPay to acquire SEC-registered North Capital in $60 million all-stock deal. The acquisition will support MoonPay’s aim of supporting mass adoption of tokenized real-world assets, CEO Ivan Soto-Wright said. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Live updates: Bitcoin pulls back to $84,000 as bond yields fly higher. The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield has soared 18 basis points on Wednesday to its highest level since 2007. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

The S&P 500 has a 'breadth' problem. Crypto doesn’t.. Your day-ahead look for Sept. 22, 2026 Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $84,317 with a -2.52% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $2,668.55 with a -3.02% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

The GENIUS Act, enacted by Congress in July 2025, created a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins whereby a subsidiary of an insured depository institution could be approved to issue payment stablecoins.

After years of opposition, the U.S. finally embraced crypto regulation in 2025.

The year 2025 proved to be a defining moment for the U.S. crypto sector. On July 18, President Donald Trump signed the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins Act, also known as the GENIUS Act, into law, creating the first comprehensive federal framework for dollar-backed stablecoins. [...] Still, progress toward clearer rules continued. In July 2025, the House passed the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act to define whether digital tokens fall under SEC or CFTC oversight.

After the ex-SEC Chair Gary Gensler resigned in January 2025, Acting Chair Mark Uyeda and the new SEC chair, Paul Atkins, pushed rules-based oversight, easing uncertainty and boosting ETF and digital asset growth.

Cryptocurrency regulation in the United States has historically been fragmented, with federal agencies applying different interpretations based on the nature and use of each asset. items.title: Cryptocurrency
items.description:
On 18 May 2021, China banned financial institutions and payment companies from being able to provide cryptocurrency transaction related services. This led to a sharp fall in the price of the biggest proof of work cryptocurrencies. For instance, bitcoin fell 31%, Ethereum fell 44%, Binance Coin fell 32% and Dogecoin fell 30%. Proof of work mining was the next focus, with regulators in popular mining regions citing the use of electricity generated from highly polluting sources such as coal to [...] ### Volatility

Cryptocurrency prices are much more volatile than established financial assets such as stocks. For example, over one week in May 2022, bitcoin lost 20% of its value and Ethereum lost 26%, while Solana "Solana (blockchain platform)") and Cardano "Cardano (blockchain platform)") lost 41% and 35% respectively. The falls were attributed to warnings about inflation. By comparison, in the same week, the Nasdaq tech stock index fell 7.6 per cent and the FTSE 100 was 3.6 per cent down. [...] In the longer term, of the 10 leading cryptocurrencies identified by the total value of coins in circulation in January 2018, only four (bitcoin, Ethereum, Cardano and Ripple "Ripple (payment protocol)") (XRP)) were still in that position in early 2022. The total value of all cryptocurrencies was $2 trillion at the end of 2021, but had halved nine months later. The Wall Street Journal has commented that the crypto sector has become "intertwined" with the rest of the capital markets and
